question.text: A smooth massless string passes over a smooth fixed pulley. Two masses $m_{1}$ and $m_{2},\left(m_{1}>m_{2}\right)$ are tied at the two ends of the string. The masses are allowed to move under gravity starting from rest. The total external force acting on the two masses is

solution.text:
We know that Acceleration, $a_{\mathrm{CM}}=\left(\frac{m_{1}-m_{2}}{m_{1}+m_{2}}\right)^{2} \times g\left(\because m_{1}>m_{2}\right)$
So, resultant external force.
$$
\begin{aligned}
F &=\left(m_{1}+m_{2}\right) a_{\mathrm{CM}} \\
&=\left(m_{1}+m_{2}\right) \times\left(\frac{m_{1}-m_{2}}{m_{1}+m_{2}}\right)^{2} \times g \\
&=\frac{\left(m_{1}-m_{2}\right)^{2}}{\left(m_{1}+m_{2}\right)} \times g
\end{aligned}
$$
